record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Determine whether there exist smooth vector fields on ℝ³ that satisfy the Markus–Yamabe hypothesis that every Jacobian matrix has eigenvalues with negative real part, yet still possess periodic orbits.

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Are there smooth vector ﬁelds in R3 under the hypotheses of the Markus–Yamabe’s conjecture and having periodic orbits?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be a smooth (i.e., $C^\infty$) vector field, and consider the autonomous differential system $\dot{x} = X(x)$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^3$. Assume that $X$ satisfies the Markus–Yamabe hypothesis: at every point $x \in \mathbb{R}^3$, all eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix $DX(x)$ have negative real part. (It is known that, despite this hypothesis, the origin need not be a global attractor when $n \ge 3$, since polynomial counterexamples to the Markus–Yamabe conjecture exist in dimension three and above.)

Determine whether there exists such a smooth vector field $X$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that admits a periodic orbit, i.e., a non-constant solution $\varphi(t)$ of $\dot{x} = X(x)$ for which there exists $T > 0$ with $\varphi(t+T) = \varphi(t)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$. Either construct such a vector field, or prove that no smooth vector field on $\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfying the Markus–Yamabe hypothesis can possess a periodic orbit.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a 2020 compendium of open problems in low-dimensional dynamical systems by Gasull. While polynomial counterexamples to the Markus–Yamabe conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$ have been constructed (Cima, Gasull, Mañosas and others), and unbounded solutions are known to occur, the specific question of whether the Markus–Yamabe hypothesis in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is compatible with the existence of periodic orbits does not appear to have been resolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: A Polynomial Counterexample to the Markus–Yamabe Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: A polynomial counterexample to the Markus–Yamabe conjecture exists in dimension n ≥ 3.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples to the Markus–Yamabe conjecture exist in R^3, but these give unbounded orbits rather than periodic ones.

status_evidence.title: Examples and counterexamples for Markus-Yamabe
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of families of vector fields in R^3 illustrating Markus–Yamabe phenomena.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature discusses related counterexamples but does not resolve the periodic orbit question.
